To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Edith Penrose never intended to contribute to the resource-based view of the firm, and that she never intended to provide useful strategy advice to practitioners.

(1) Penrose’s theory is not directly about rents, but is about the processes of growth; (2) Penrose was a micro-economist who was concerned with efficiency; (3) Penrose’s micro-level theory was not intended to have implications for the macro-level; (4) Penrose did not consider that rents were possible; and (5) Penrose did consider that rents could arise, but only as a macro-level outcome of a micro-level process that was efficient
